- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward bias by +1–1.5% to align with true mean reversion.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true peak); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean tends to drift higher than true mean in 30-day horizon; apply a “mean reversion” penalty: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast average if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum reversal; adjust forecast slope to match sentiment swing direction (e.g., if sentiment shifts from +0.67 to -0.33, reduce slope by 10–15%).
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes; apply a 7-day smoothing filter to sentiment before weighting forecast adjustments.
